question: Does one-worker Search receive stable execution time despite the persistent approximately1.2 global busy logical CPUs that have blocked every frozen1.0-core admission before any game? Contract requires qualified contention, not this investigator-selected numerical limit. A failed old admission remains failed; this is an outcome-independent challenge to a resource premise, not a change to played evidence.
design: First12 full-history played-corpus roots, baseline/verified-null/nominal-verified-null,1worker/Hash64/ADAPTIVE16/frozen CP64. One complete warmup round and two measured rounds, rotated profile order by root/round,1M-node/D40 requests. Record elapsed, owner CPU, process CPU, GC/JIT, completion/nodes/score/PV and native lifetime/global host interval. No concurrent research or game; BelowNormal, ActiveProcessorCount4, Xms256m/Xmx1024m. This measures scheduling plus JVM pauses; it does not attribute every lost CPU opportunity or establish perfect isolation.
rationale: At least90% median execution delivery with bounded lower tail and at most5 percentage-point profile separation is a practical non-starvation screen; one serial W1 game on6physical/12logical cores with at most2 other logical cores and8GiB free is background-friendly. These are prospective operating tolerances, not statistical proof of no contention. CPU quantization, GC/JIT and short bursts remain limitations; no profile or request may be dropped after measurement.
decision: If every criterion passes, a NEW unplayed clock protocol may use2.0 global other-core admission plus the same memory gates, a pre/post CPU-delivery check, and whole-match per-actor nativeCPU/whole-request elapsed resource checks frozen before games.
